content: Rilpivirine does not require dose adjustment when co-administered with other medications. However, clinical monitoring is essential in various scenarios due to potential drug-drug interactions, particularly those affecting the QTc interval or hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Below are detailed considerations for specific interactions: 1. Azole Antifungals: Co-administration with rilpivirine may increase the risk of breakthrough fungal infections. Monitor patients closely. 2. Lapatinib: Rilpivirine increases lapatinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 3. Drugs with Torsades de Pointes Risk: Rilpivirine should be used cautiously with drugs known to increase the risk of Torsades de Pointes. 4. Levofloxacin: Rilpivirine increases levofloxacin toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 5. Levoketoconazole: This drug increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity, but no dose adjustment is required. 6. Lithium: Both rilpivirine and lithium prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 7. Lopinavir: Lopinavir increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, while rilpivirine increases lopinavir toxicity through QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 8. Lumefantrine: Rilpivirine increases lumefantrine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 9. Magnesium Salts (Chloride, Gluconate, Oxide, Sulfate): These agents decrease rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 10. Methadone: Rilpivirine increases methadone toxicity via QTc prolongation. No dose adjustment is required, but monitor closely. 11. Mirtazapine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 12. Moxifloxacin: Rilpivirine increases moxifloxacin toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 13. Nefazodone: This drug increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity. 14. Nelfinavir: Nelfinavir increases rilpivirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Nizatidine: This H2 antagonist decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 17. Nortriptyline: Rilpivirine increases nortriptyline toxicity via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 18. Octreotide: Rilpivirine increases octreotide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 19. Ofloxacin: Rilpivirine increases ofloxacin toxicity via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 20. Olanzapine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 21. Orlistat: Orlistat decreases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, potentially leading to virological failure. Monitor HIV RNA levels frequently and discontinue orlistat if viral load increases. 22. Osilodrostat: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 23. Ozanimod: Additive effects on heart rate and QTc prolongation may occur. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients on QT-prolonging drugs. 24. Paliperidone: Rilpivirine increases paliperidone toxicity via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 25. Pazopanib: Rilpivirine increases pazopanib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 26. Pentamidine: Rilpivirine increases pentamidine toxicity via QTc prolongation. Use caution and monitor. 27. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 30. Primaquine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 31. Procainamide: Rilpivirine increases procainamide toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 32. Propafenone: Rilpivirine increases propafenone toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 33. Protriptyline: Rilpivirine increases protriptyline toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 34. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 55. Trimipramine: Rilpivirine increases trimipramine toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 56. Ublituximab: This drug decreases rilpivirine effects due to immunosuppressive effects, increasing infection risk. Monitor closely. 57. Valbenazine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 58. Vandetanib: Rilpivirine increases vandetanib toxicity via QTc prolongation. Monitor closely. 59. Voclosporin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor. 60. Voriconazole: This drug increases rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. No dose adjustment is required, but monitor for toxicity. In all cases, careful monitoring of QTc intervals and plasma concentrations is critical to mitigate risks of toxicity or therapeutic failure.
